description: Effect of sourcing the profit-shifted share on the lever ranking. The parameter was swept over a judgement range because only one source had been obtained; a second was found on 2026-10-06 measuring the same object.

before.note: At this width the ranking was unstable: widening to 0.48 plus or minus 0.16 moved profit shifting to second and 0.48 plus or minus 0.19 moved it to first.

after.basis: two independent sources on the same denominator

sources: Torslov, Wier and Zucman (2023), The Missing Profits of Nations: 48 percent of the pre-tax profit of majority-owned foreign affiliates of US multinationals was booked in tax havens in 2016, from the BEA value added tables.
Garcia-Bernardo, Jansky and Zucman (2022), NBER w30086, abstract verified verbatim: 'The share of foreign profits booked in tax havens remained stable around 50% between 2015 and 2020.'
denominator_caveat: Both sources measure a share of FOREIGN profits. The assembly applies the parameter to the whole rent base. That overstates shifting unless essentially all rent is earned through foreign affiliates; correcting it would raise tau_k and narrow the measured shortfall. Reported as a limitation rather than silently changed.
correction: An earlier note sought 'Clausing (NBER w28442)'. NBER w28442 is Solar Geoengineering, Learning, and Experimentation, not a profit-shifting paper.
